c.tagline: A canal city where skyscrapers meet the jungle.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are largely zone-based/negotiated flat rates rather than metered; confirm the price before getting in, or use an app (Uber/Cabify) for a fixed upfront fare.

emergency.note: 911 is Panama's unified national emergency number; SUME 911 dispatches ambulances.

avoid.reason: Stay out of El Chorrillo, Curundú and the back streets of Santa Ana, which have serious gang crime, and take care where Casco Viejo's fringes meet them.
Petty theft occurs on Avenida Central and in Casco Viejo after dark; use ride-hailing apps or registered taxis rather than flagging cabs on the street.

hood_desc: UNESCO-listed old town with cobblestone streets, restored colonial mansions, rooftop bars, and boutique/backpacker lodging; ideal for first-time visitors and nightlife/culture seekers.
Central, walkable district near embassies, Via Argentina's cafes, and a metro station; popular with backpackers and budget travelers wanting easy transit access.
Leafy commercial-residential area bridging Casco Viejo and the financial district, with solid mid-range hotels and strong local dining; good for a quieter, well-connected base.
Nightlife and dining hub centered on Calle Uruguay, walking distance to the financial district's bars, clubs and restaurants; suits visitors who want to be in the action.
Upscale high-rise district by the bay near Multiplaza mall and top hospitals, with modern luxury towers; suits business travelers and those wanting resort-style comfort.

water.note: Tap water in the city center and hotel zones is treated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Metro and Metrobus fares are paid with a rechargeable smart Metro Card (tarjeta multimodal) tapped at turnstiles or bus fareboxes; cards are sold and topped up with cash at metro stations and many convenience stores. Cash is not accepted directly on buses or at metro gates.
transit.hours: Metro and Metrobus run roughly 5am-11pm daily with reduced Sunday service; overnight, rely on taxis or rideshare apps like Uber and Cabify.
transit.note: Metro Lines 1 and 2 (with Line 3 expanding west) cover downtown and the suburbs but do not reach Tocumen airport directly, so pair it with Metrobus or a taxi for that leg.

tip.r: About 10% at sit-down restaurants is customary; some bills already add a service charge, so check before tipping twice. Tipping taxi/rideshare drivers is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Panama Canal (Miraflores Locks)

Watch massive cargo ships rise and fall through this engineering marvel that reshaped global trade forever. The visitor center's observation deck offers a front-row seat to one of humanity's greatest feats of engineering.
Casco Viejo

Panama City's colonial old quarter charms with pastel facades, wrought-iron balconies, and plazas buzzing with salsa music and rooftop bars. Its cobblestone streets blend Spanish, French, and Afro-Caribbean influences into one vibrant UNESCO-listed neighborhood.
Panama City Skyline (Cinta Costera)

The glittering high-rise skyline along the bay, best viewed from the Cinta Costera waterfront promenade, has earned Panama City the nickname 'Dubai of Central America.' Sunset transforms the skyscrapers into a shimmering silhouette.
Amador Causeway

This scenic road connects four small islands and offers sweeping views of both the city skyline and the Pacific entrance to the canal. It's a favorite for biking, dining, and watching ships queue for passage.
Panama Viejo

The evocative ruins of the original Panama City, founded in 1519 and later destroyed by the pirate Henry Morgan, stand as a UNESCO World Heritage archaeological site. Climb the old cathedral tower for views over the ruins and modern skyline beyond.
Biomuseo

Designed by architect Frank Gehry, this vividly colored museum tells the story of how the Isthmus of Panama transformed the planet's biodiversity. Its bold, angular architecture is a landmark in itself along the causeway.
Metropolitan Natural Park

A rare slice of tropical rainforest within city limits, this park offers hiking trails alive with sloths, toucans, and howler monkeys just minutes from downtown skyscrapers. Its lookout point delivers a striking city-meets-jungle panorama.
Cathedral Basilica Santa María la Antigua

Anchoring Casco Viejo's Plaza de la Independencia, this beautifully restored cathedral features a mother-of-pearl-inlaid facade and twin bell towers. It's a serene centerpiece of the old town's colonial charm.
Ancon Hill

This forested hill offers the best panoramic view of Panama City, the canal, and the surrounding bay, all crowned by a giant Panamanian flag. It's a favorite sunrise hike for both locals and visitors.
Mercado de Mariscos (Fish Market)
This bustling harborside market serves some of the freshest ceviche in Central America alongside piles of the day's catch. It's an authentic, flavorful window into Panama City's coastal culture.

train.note: Panama has no national passenger rail network and no international trains. The only passenger train is the Panama Canal Railway, a scenic trans-isthmus tourist/commuter service between Panama City (Corozal/Albrook) and Colon, running early weekday mornings; book by phone/email via panarail.com.

intl.to: Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, El Salvador, Guatemala & Tapachula (Mexico)

bus.note: International coaches leave from Albrook Terminal and run only north through Central America, since the Darien Gap means there is no road link to Colombia. Bring your passport; the Costa Rica crossing is at Paso Canoas.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled international passenger ferry to Colombia; the former Ferry Xpress service ended and the sea route to Cartagena is now only backpacker sailboats via the San Blas islands. Domestic ferries run from the Amador causeway area to Isla Taboga (Taboga Express, https://tabogaexpress.com/) and to the Pearl Islands.
